Chemi-Ion Driven Flows in a Time Varying
Electric Field
Jesse Tinajero1
Derek Dunn-Rankin1
Jie Bia2
Miguel Plascencia1
1Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering,
University of California-Irvine
2School of Marine Engineering,
Northwestern Polytechnical University
ASGSR - October 26th, 2014
ASGSR 2014, Pasadena
Chemi-Ion Driven Flows in a Time Varying Electric Field

Motivation
I Preparation for 2016-17 micro-gravity experiments on-board the ISS via
Nasa’s ACME (Advanced Combustion Via Microgravity Experiments)
I Study the transient effect of chemi-ions in the bulk gas
I Study the effects of important parameters (i.e. ﬁeld strength and electrode
gap distance) that characterize electric ﬁeld combustion (i.e. time-scales
and length-scales) in a transient state
I Acquire full dynamic control of combustion using electric ﬁelds

Conclusions
1. Transient Effects due to Voltage Steps
I A wave is created in thermal plume. The wave is more apparent near
satuartion ﬁelds and for longer electrode spacings.
I Average plume wave velocity was linear with average ﬁeld strength
I 75hz oscillation appears in the ion current measurements when ﬁeld strength
surpasses 2kV/cm. This oscillation can clearly be seen in the schlieren
videos
2. Time-Scales
I UCI H.V. power supply produces electrode potential on the order of a 1kV in
2-3ms. The ACME H.V. power supply produces the same electrode potential
at a rate 0.1kV/ms
I Bulk of ion current arrives downstream at ⇡10-20ms
I Plume reaction time for a voltage step from the UCI power supply was
⇡2-3ms. The plume reaction time for the ACME power supply was seen to
be longer
